football_evidence.question: Can Wyoming’s pass rush get to Taron Dickens?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Wyoming, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.7 of the 4.1 points, but not the full gap. Input warning: EdgeDesk’s published number sits 9.2 points from the middle of its own other models. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Wyoming has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Wyoming’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 11.3% of its runs, and Northern Illinois’ defense stops 9.9% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Northern Illinois has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Northern Illinois’ offense has allowed a sack on 10.2% of its dropbacks, and Wyoming’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Northern Illinois has the ball (big plays through the air): Northern Illinois’ offense turns 9.2% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Wyoming’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).
Jalen Macon has completed 5 of 12 passes (41.7%) for 20 yards, 1.7 yards per attempt, no touchdowns and no interceptions in two games for Northern Illinois, and has been sacked on 3 of 15 dropbacks.
contradicting: When Wyoming has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Wyoming’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.9% of its dropbacks, and Northern Illinois’ defense sacks the quarterback on 5.2% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Wyoming has the ball (big plays through the air): Wyoming’s offense turns 7.6% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Northern Illinois’ defense gives up explosive gains on 9.7% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.4%).
In his last two games (North Dakota State and San José State), Hughes averaged 4.4 yards per attempt, against 6.8 in his four games before that.

When Wyoming has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Wyoming’s offense averages 6.4 yards per pass attempt, and Northern Illinois’ defense allows 7.9 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.5).
quarterbacks: Tyler Hughes has completed 82 of 136 passes (60.3%) for 834 yards, 6.1 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 7 interceptions in six games for Wyoming, and has been sacked on 14 of 150 dropbacks.

Taron Dickens has completed 97 of 140 passes (69.3%) for 977 yards, 7.0 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in five games for Northern Illinois, and has been sacked on 15 of 155 dropbacks.
Jalen Macon has completed 5 of 12 passes (41.7%) for 20 yards, 1.7 yards per attempt, no touchdowns and no interceptions in two games for Northern Illinois, and has been sacked on 3 of 15 dropbacks.
